tagline: Grammar, clarity, tone, and AI writing assistant across apps.
verdictSummary: Grammar checking itself is a solved, open-source problem, and wiring it to an LLM for tone rewrites is a real weekend build. What doesn't come with it is Grammarly's actual product: suggestions appearing inline inside every app you already write in, not a separate page you paste text into.
coreLoopDIY: Run text through a local open-source grammar engine plus an optional LLM rewrite pass, in a page you paste your writing into.
whatYouLose: inline suggestions inside Gmail, Docs, Slack, and everywhere else you write
tone and brand controls tuned for an organization
years of tuning down false-positive suggestions
whyPeopleStillPay: The value is suggestions appearing inside the apps where writing actually happens — a destination you paste into is a real downgrade from that, even with equally good grammar checking underneath.
notes: An important 'kinda': grammar checking itself is open source; cross-app inline UX is the actual hard product.
prompt:
Build a personal writing checker around LanguageTool, an open-source grammar and style engine you can run locally via its official Docker image — grammar checks never have to leave your machine. Build a small page where you paste text and see LanguageTool's issues underlined with hover explanations and click-to-apply suggestions. Add an LLM-powered rewrite pane with a few fixed options (tighten, friendlier, more formal) that shows a diff against the original before anything is applied — never silently overwrite the source text. Support a personal dictionary file of names and jargon that should never be flagged, passed into every check. Add a command-line mode that checks a file and exits non-zero on any issue, so it can run as a pre-commit hook on documentation.

Do not build a browser extension or inline suggestions inside Gmail, Docs, or Slack — that cross-app integration is real, ongoing platform work, and this build is honestly a destination you paste into, not a layer over everything else.

faq.q: Can I bring over anything from my Grammarly account?
faq.a: Not really — Grammarly doesn't export your personal dictionary or writing style settings. Rebuilding your ignore-list of names and jargon is quick, but it starts from scratch.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: As a page you paste text into, technically yes, but there's no inline suggestion layer and no keyboard integration — on mobile specifically, that gap is much more noticeable than on desktop.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting for LanguageTool, which wants roughly a gigabyte of memory, plus optional LLM API usage for the rewrite feature — a few dollars a month either way.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Writing where you already write. Grammarly's suggestions appear inside Gmail, Docs, and Slack as you type; this build only ever sees text you've copied somewhere else first.
